title: Stand a glass unit on two setting blocks in a window frame channel
instruction: Stand the glass unit centred in the frame on the two black setting blocks, set on the white marks, and let go. The glass must never touch the sill.
context: General maintenance and repair workers (about 1.6 million in the US, BLS occupation 49-9071) keep buildings in repair, and replacing a broken or misted glazed unit in a window or door is part of that work. On the job the worker takes off the beads, lifts out the failed unit, checks or renews the setting blocks and stands the new unit on them in the existing frame; this task is that last step. The unit stands on two setting blocks at its quarter points, so its weight never bears on the sill; glass whose bottom edge comes down on the sill can chip, crack or lose its seal. The hard part is the descent: the 24 mm unit goes over stops 40 mm tall into a 40 mm channel (8 mm per side) and down onto blocks whose tops are 9 mm above the sill, without touching the sill. The order of work is left to the robot. One arm reaches the blocks, the other the glass. Glass still held, or hovering above the blocks, is not resting on them.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Five kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Frame: the bottom of a window frame in grey (sRGB 0.60, 0.62, 0.65) aluminium, fixed to the table, centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0: a sill 60 mm along x, 260 mm along y and 10 mm tall; standing on the sill, two glazing stops (walls 8 mm thick along x, 260 mm long along y, 40 mm tall) whose inner faces are at x 28.0 and 32.0 cm, leaving a 40 mm wide channel along y with its floor (the sill's top) 10 mm above the table and the stops' tops 50 mm above it; and two jambs (40 mm along x, 10 mm along y, 60 mm tall) standing on the sill between the stops with their inner faces at y -12.0 and +12.0 cm, closing the channel's ends, so the channel is 240 mm long and open at the top. (2) Two quarter-point marks: thin white (sRGB 0.95, 0.95, 0.95) plastic plates, 24 mm along x, 30 mm along y and 1 mm thick, fixed on the sill in the channel, centred at x 30.0 cm, y -5.0 and +5.0 cm (the quarter points of a 200 mm unit centred in the channel). (3) Block tray: a dark grey (sRGB 0.30, 0.30, 0.32) plastic plate 90 x 90 x 4 mm, fixed, centred at x 20.0 cm, y -24.0 cm. (4) Two setting blocks: loose black (sRGB 0.08, 0.08, 0.08) neoprene rubber blocks, 24 mm along x, 30 mm along y and 8 mm tall, 7 g each, lying flat on the tray side by side, centred at x 18.0 and 22.0 cm, y -24.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y. (5) Glass unit: a loose small double-glazed unit (two 2 mm panes on a 20 mm aluminium spacer), 24 mm thick, 200 mm long and 80 mm tall, 0.20 kg, pale blue-grey (sRGB 0.75, 0.85, 0.90), standing on one of its 24 x 200 mm long edges on the table, centred at x 22.0 cm, y +29.0 cm (its ends at y +19.0 and +39.0 cm), its length along y and its faces normal to x; for real trials, acrylic panes on a weighted spacer, of the same size and mass, are safer than glass. With a top-down grasp only the right arm reaches the blocks and only the left arm reaches the glass unit: near the table the left arm reaches no further right than about y -18 cm at x 18 cm, short of the blocks' nearer sides at y -22.5 cm, and the right arm no further left than about y +17 cm at x 21 cm, short of the unit's nearer end at y +19 cm. An arm stretched across with its gripper turned sideways could reach further. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Read every control step (20 Hz): the objects' poses and both arms (TCP, pad tips, gripper opening). 'The channel': between the stops' and the jambs' inner faces (x 28.0 to 32.0 cm, y -12.0 to +12.0 cm). 'Touched the sill': at some step some part of the glass unit inside the channel's outline (2 mm slack) was in contact with the sill's top or a mark's top (0.5 mm or less above the surface under it; a near miss is not a touch). An object is 'let go' when on each of the last 20 control steps (1 s) both grippers' finger zones (README) were 30 mm or more from it; a step with unreadable arms or an uncomputable distance restarts the count for all. It is 'still' when each of its poses over those 20 steps is within 2 mm and 2 degrees of the current one. 'Tilt': the angle of the unit's 80 mm height axis from vertical; 'standing in the channel': all eight corners inside the channel's outline from above (1 mm slack), tilt under 3 degrees. A block 'lies on the sill' when its 8 mm axis is within 10 degrees of vertical, its lowest point within 1 mm of the sill's or a mark's top and its centre inside the channel. It is 'set' on a mark when it lies on the sill, is let go and still, its sides are within 15 degrees of the channel's and its centre is within 8 mm of the mark's centre; 'both blocks set': one on each mark. The unit 'rests on' a block only when the unit and that block are both let go and still, the block lies on the sill, at least half of the block's top is under the unit (seen from above), and the underside is within 1 mm of the block's top there (above or below): a held unit, or one more than 1 mm up, rests on nothing. 'Off centre': the unit's centre from the channel's, along y. Score 0 if the unit touched the sill at any moment or if at the end it is tilted over 30 degrees or off the table (lowest point over 10 mm below the table top). Otherwise: 1.0 if both blocks are set and the unit stands in the channel resting on both, at most 8 mm off centre; 0.75 if it stands in the channel resting on both, the blocks are within 20 mm of their marks' centres (one on each, let go and still, sides within 15 degrees) and it is at most 15 mm off centre, short of 1.0; 0.5 if it stands in the channel resting on at least one block, short of 0.75; 0.25 if both blocks are set but the unit does not stand in the channel resting on a block (not brought over, held, hovering, leaning); else 0. Read at the last step; the trial ends early (success) once the 1.0 conditions, everything let go and still included, have held for 1 s. Real trial: blue marking chalk on all four edges of the unit; a print on the sill or on a white mark shows a touch. After the end photo and video the unit is lifted straight out and the channel photographed from above: block-to-mark distance, block turn and any chalk print on the sill or a mark are read on that photo; ruler and protractor on the end photo give the unit's centre distance and tilt; the video shows the 30 mm release and the 1 s stillness; resting means the unit stands on its own, let go and still for 1 s, with no chalk print on the sill or marks, so only the blocks carry it.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction, 20 Hz. Simplified: the glass unit is one uniform box of its stated size and mass; the blocks are rigid, 30 mm long so two fit at the unit's quarter points. The frame is cut down to its bottom rail with both stops fixed, so the unit goes in from above instead of being tilted in from the room side before the bead is refitted; the setting-block step is the same. Not modelled: beads, tape, sealant, breakage, contact forces.
reset_notes: Put the two setting blocks back flat on the tray, centred at x 18.0 and 22.0 cm, y -24.0 cm, their 30 mm sides along y, and the glass unit back standing on a long edge on the table, centred at x 22.0 cm, y +29.0 cm, its faces normal to x. Nothing is consumed (in a real build, wipe any chalk off the sill).
